title: Autoformalization of mathematical reasoning
bottleneck: Frontier models can sketch proofs in natural language but cannot reliably translate them into machine-checkable formal proofs — the step that would make AI mathematics trustworthy. The UnsolvedMath benchmark found models do strong literature search but none can autoformalize; extended thinking helps on simple problems, while global mental picture, systematic self-verification, and analogical reasoning remain absent. Proof assistants demand a precision LLMs don't have. Manual formalization takes experts months per theorem, so the verification gap bottlenecks the entire AI-math pipeline.
why_it_blocks: Without formalization, AI-generated mathematics cannot be verified except by scarce human experts, capping the speed of AI-assisted discovery.
current_state: Lean and Isabelle copilots assist human formalizers, but end-to-end autoformalization of novel proofs is unsolved. Each model generation improves informal reasoning far faster than formalization ability.
